dedupe_keys.name: 100 m population grid in the conus by disaggregating census data with open source microsoft building footprints

description: Huang and colleagues provide a 100 m population grid for the contiguous United States. They disaggregate American Community Survey 2013–2017 five-year population estimates using Microsoft building footprints released in 2018, with OpenStreetMap information to remove non-residential footprints. Harvard Dataverse hosts version 2 of the product under CC0 and lists a 2.5 GB PopGrid.tif plus small sidecar files. The grid can help place population demand and exposure near transport links, health services or emergency shelters when a simulation needs finer detail than census tracts. The pixel values are modelled allocations of survey estimates, not a household count or a current census. Building extraction errors, land-use filtering and the older survey period can affect local results. The article reports the raster size and method, while the Dataverse page confirms the public release, licence and file listing. No TIFF was downloaded, so cell values, coordinate system and nodata treatment were not independently checked.
